title: Learning to Optimize by Differentiable Programming
abstract: arXiv:2601.16510v5 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Solving massive-scale optimization problems requires scalable first-order methods with low per-iteration cost. This tutorial highlights a shift in optimization: using differentiable programming not only to execute algorithms but to learn how to design them. Modern frameworks such as PyTorch, TensorFlow, and JAX enable this paradigm through efficient automatic differentiation. Embedding first-order methods within these systems allows end-to-end training that improves convergence and solution quality. Guided by Fenchel-Rockafellar duality, the tutorial demonstrates how duality-informed iterative schemes such as the alternating direction method of multipliers, and the primal-dual hybrid gradient can be learned and adapted through representative case studies.

translated_title: 通过可微编程学习优化
translated_abstract: 求解大规模优化问题需要具有低单次迭代成本的可扩展一阶方法。本教程重点介绍了优化领域的一个转变：使用可微编程不仅用于执行算法，还用于学习如何设计算法。PyTorch、TensorFlow 和 JAX 等现代框架通过高效的自动微分实现了这一范式。将一阶方法嵌入这些系统中可以实现端到端训练，从而提升收敛性和解的质量。在 Fenchel-Rockafellar 对偶理论的指导下，本教程通过代表性案例研究展示了如何学习和调整对偶信息引导的迭代方案，例如交替方向乘子法（ADMM）和原始-对偶混合梯度法（PDHG）。
tldr: 本教程展示了如何利用可微编程框架（如PyTorch、TensorFlow和JAX）通过端到端训练来学习和设计一阶优化方法（如ADMM和原始-对偶混合梯度法），从而提升收敛性和解的质量。
en_tdlr: This tutorial demonstrates how differentiable programming frameworks (e.g., PyTorch, TensorFlow, JAX) enable learning and designing first-order optimization methods such as ADMM and primal-dual hybrid gradient through end-to-end training, guided by Fenchel-Rockafellar duality.
